texts.preamble: Balaraj A vs Sanjay S N on 29 October, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.6547/2023 Kabc0B0161952023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 29th Day of October 2024 M.V.C. No.6547/2023 Petitioner/s: 1. Sri. A. Balaraj S/o C. Anthonappa, Aged about 65 years, R/at Sannenahalli, Masavanaghatta Post, Tiptur Taluk, Tumkur-572224.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 12.04.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.04.2023 at about 9.25 p.m., petitioner was riding TVS Moped bearing Reg. No. KA- 50-W-2046 slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations by observing on moving vehicles and by wearing head guard on Channarayapatna Srinivasapura Road, when reached near Sasalpura Cross, at that time one Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 13-EV-4959 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came to main road at a high speed from Salsapur and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle. Due to the impact, petitioner sustained grevious injuries. Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Channarayapatna, wherein first aid treatment was given and further shifted to Punya Hospital, Hassan, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 65 years, the petitioner was working as Coolie and earning Rs.750/- per day. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent. Hence, placed exparte. Balaraj A vs Sanjay S N on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174178886/ 2 The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 149(2), 134(c), 158(6) and 170 of M. V. Act. Further the complaint is lodged on 13.04.2023 i.e., after lapse of 1 day from the date of alleged accident. Further this respondent submits that, the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident. Further this respondent submits that, the driver of Motorcycle bearing No. KA-13-EV-4959 was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the particular class of vehicle as on the date of the accident. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15 and also examined Dr. Mahesh. V as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.16 and P.17 and closed their side.
texts.arguments: 15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
